text:
sara: Quick follow-up from the onboarding pipeline RFC — I think we should add a lightweight "sample_weight" field to the model descriptor so bench can reconstruct realistic seqlen/latency distributions without heavy re-ingest. Short notes + tradeoffs below.
sara: TL;DR: small API bump, less rework in bench, but risk of inconsistent weights across teams if we make them optional.
ravi: Can you sketch the descriptor shape?
sara: Sure, proposal snippet:
```json
{
  \"model_id\": \"meta/my-model:1.0\",
  \"tokenizer_fingerprint\": \"sha1:abcd1234\",
  \"sample_weight\": [ { \"seqlen\": 16, \"pct\": 0.5 }, { \"seqlen\": 128, \"pct\": 0.3 }, { \"seqlen\": 512, \"pct\": 0.2 } ]
}
```
ravi: Nice. Question: will bench trust these weights or use them as hints? If trusted we can resample less, but risk bad coverage.
jia: My preference: treat as hints but add a validation step that compares observed production seqlen histogram over a week and emits a drift alert if KL divergence > threshold.
tom: Also need a compatibility field for runtime/quant binaries. We've seen subtle failures when quantized kernel ABI changes. Something like `quant_abi_version` and `runtime_compat` flags?
sara: Agree. Add `quant_abi_version` string and `required_runtime_features` list. Example: `required_runtime_features: [\"kv-seq-opt\", \"fused-attn-v2\"]`.
margo: From cost + telemetry POV: we should also include a `bench_budget` (approx token-hours) so onboarding can gate heavy deep-benches. Otherwise large models eat our slot pool during intake.
ravi: Gate semantics: if bench_budget > X, kickoff deep bench only on dedicated canary infra; otherwise run lightweight smokes. We should expose a canary flag: `onboard.canary_mode=true` to control traffic routing.
jia: Edgecase: tokenizers that change offsets (esp. non-BPE). We must require `tokenizer_fingerprint` or else block admission. Otherwise eval diffs become impossible to interpret.
sara: Good catch. Proposed admission rules:
- tokenizer_fingerprint must be present and validated by ingest.
- sample_weight optional but defaults to cluster-wide seqlen distribution if absent.
- quant_abi_version required for any quantized binaries.
- bench_budget caps deep benchmark scheduling.
- telemetry tag `owner` required for alert routing.
These live in the `admit` contract and will be enforced by the intake service.
admit-bot: [automated] ran quick-check: model meta/my-model:1.0 - tokenizer_fingerprint missing -> FAIL (see /admit/logs/6123456789).
margo: That bot catch shows why we need a good UX. When a descriptor fails, the bot should return an actionable checklist: missing fields, suggested defaults, and a dry-run command to run local smoke.
tom: For UX, add a `admit-cli` command snippet in errors: `redwood-admit validate path/to/descriptor.json --dry-run`. Also produce a minimal local smoke harness: `./smoke.sh --model meta/my-model:1.0 --quick`.
ravi: On rollout: start by making `sample_weight` optional and treat as hint. After 6 weeks of telemetry and a small pilot, flip to required for new models. Backfill existing models by auto-suggesting weights from production traces.
jia: About evaluation: bench should tag results with `descriptor_hash` and `tokenizer_fingerprint` so we can match regressions to tokenizer/descriptor changes. Important for regression triage.
sara: Interface boundary question: who owns the mapping from descriptor -> bench config? Option A: intake service translates descriptor to bench-config. Option B: bench maintains mapping rules and pulls descriptor. I lean A (single source at intake), but bench team may want control. Thoughts?
tom: I prefer A for correctness (intake has the context). Bench can subscribe to descriptors but intake should emit canonical bench-config.
margo: Agree — intake emits `bench_config_v1` artifact stored in catalog; bench workers pick jobs from that artifact. Makes audit and replay easier.
ravi: Last practical: add a `compatibility_score` field returned by the validator (0..100) and a small human-readable `compat_notes` string for edge cases. If score < 60 require manual review.
sara: Great. Action items:
- sara: draft updated descriptor schema in repo (PR) by EOD Wed.
- ravi + tom: design admit-bot error UX + CLI snippet by next Tue.
- jia: telemetry alert KL threshold proposal by end of week.
- margo: bench_budget defaults and scheduling policy doc next Wed.
- admit-bot: include dry-run link and logs in future failures.
Anyone want to be added as reviewer/owner?
ravi: I'll review schema + own rollout plan.
jia: I'll review telemetry.
margo: I'll scout cost caps.
sara: Thanks all :thumbsup:
